question.prompt: How many distinct values of \(x\) satisfy \[\lfloor x \rfloor^2 - 3x + 2 = 0,\] where \(\lfloor x \rfloor\) denotes the largest integer less than or equal to \(x?\)

solutions.title: Restrict the integer part
solutions.explanation:
The equation gives \(3x=\lfloor x\rfloor^2+2\ge2\), so \(x\ge2/3\). This immediately rules out negative values of the floor.

Set \(n=\lfloor x\rfloor\). Then \(n\) is a nonnegative integer, and the equation determines
\[
x=\frac{n^2+2}{3}.
\]
We must also respect the defining interval \(n\le x<n+1\). In particular,
\[
\frac{n^2+2}{3}<n+1
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad n(n-3)<1.
\]
If \(n\ge4\), then \(n(n-3)\ge4\), which is impossible. Thus only \(n=0,1,2,3\) need to be checked.

Substitution gives the pairs
\[
(n,x)=\left(0,\frac23\right),\ (1,1),\ (2,2),\ \left(3,\frac{11}{3}\right).
\]
In each pair, \(n\le x<n+1\), so the floor really is \(n\). Each possible floor value determines only one candidate, and the four candidates are distinct. Therefore there are \(\boxed{4}\) solutions, choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).

solutions.title: Use the fractional part and parity
solutions.explanation:
Separating the integer and fractional parts produces a product of consecutive integers, whose parity sharply limits the possibilities.

Write \(x=n+f\), where \(n=\lfloor x\rfloor\) is an integer and \(0\le f<1\). Substituting into the equation gives
\[
n^2-3n+2=3f,
\qquad (n-1)(n-2)=3f.
\]
One of the consecutive integers \(n-1,n-2\) is even, so their product is an even integer. Since \(0\le3f<3\), that product can only be \(0\) or \(2\).

If the product is \(0\), then \(n=1\) or \(2\), and \(f=0\). This gives \(x=1,2\).

If the product is \(2\), then
\[
n^2-3n+2=2
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad n(n-3)=0.
\]
Thus \(n=0\) or \(3\), and \(f=2/3\). This gives \(x=2/3,11/3\).

All four constructions have \(0\le f<1\), so their floor values are correct. The exhaustive cases give \(\boxed{4}\) distinct solutions, choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
